## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Short-dated Treasuries gave back part of their haven rally as Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia revived confidence in artificial-intelligence investment and restored expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate increase. Falling oil prices supported the long end, leaving a sharply flatter curve: the two-year yield rose 4.69 basis points to 4.6938%, the 10-year was virtually unchanged at 4.9437%, and the 30-year fell 2.3 basis points to 5.3068%.

The recovery in risk appetite reached corporate debt, where technology bonds rebounded and credit-protection costs declined. Yet the Treasury response was restrained compared with the 4.73% surge in the S&P 500 and 6.86% advance in the Nasdaq 100. Cheaper energy reduced inflation compensation while real yields rose, preserving an important distinction between relief from the oil shock and the underlying cost of financing investment.

New York Fed President John Williams maintained the case for further action against inflation, while fresh U.S. business surveys showed slower expansion alongside continued hiring and elevated costs. The session brought renewed confidence in the AI industry's leadership without an equivalent retreat from monetary restraint.

## Treasury Flattening Accompanies Slower U.S. Activity

The recovery began before the U.S. cash opening, with equity futures rebounding from the previous week's technology rout. Nvidia's board then reinstated Huang with immediate effect after receiving input from senior levels of the U.S. government. President Donald Trump endorsed the decision. Nvidia shares gained about 31%, and semiconductor stocks finished 14.03% higher, reversing much of the immediate pressure on the industry's market valuations.

Floodlines Research strategist Anna Wu described investors withdrawing some of the safety demand that had supported Treasuries during the AI selloff. Policy-sensitive yields rose as traders rebuilt tightening expectations. Bloomberg's Monday rates account said futures again fully reflected a quarter-point Fed increase in December, with little support for a larger half-point move. That restored a degree of policy restraint that Friday's flight from risk had removed from prices.

The adjustment diminished along the curve. Five-year yields rose 2.15 basis points to 4.7618%, while the 10-year edged down just 0.01 basis point. The two- to 10-year spread narrowed 4.7 basis points to 24.99 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap contracted 6.99 basis points to 61.3. Even after the front-end setback, two-year yields remained 13.56 basis points below November 16, against an 18.74-basis-point decline at 10 years. Monday reversed only part of the recent Treasury recovery.

Oil supplied the other major influence on the curve. WTI futures fell 3.79% to $80.25 a barrel and Brent declined 3.49% to $89.34, taking their monthly losses to about 20%. Bloomberg's rates reporting linked the commodity decline to lower inflation compensation and support for longer government bonds, including European debt. Treasury futures activity was unusually heavy: through 3 p.m. New York, volume in most contracts was at least 15% above its 20-day average.

At 10 years, inflation compensation fell 2.4 basis points to 2.1428%, almost exactly offsetting a 2.39-basis-point increase in the real yield to 2.8009%. The monthly comparison makes the separation more pronounced. The breakeven was 21.02 basis points lower, while the real yield was 15.94 basis points higher. The nominal yield's 5.08-basis-point monthly decline consequently coexisted with a higher inflation-adjusted financing cost.

Williams' Monday remarks supplied a fresh policy assessment during that repricing. He said the economy remained strong and inflation too high, requiring action over time to restore the 2% objective sustainably. He projected real growth of about 2.75% in both 2026 and 2027, with unemployment declining from 4.1% toward 4% next year. His inflation forecast put this year's rate at 3.5%, next year's slightly above 2%, and a return to target in 2028. Risks to inflation remained tilted upward, and his December 8-9 decision would depend on incoming data.

His account also distinguished price increases in particular industries from broader persistence. Tariff effects had largely abated, housing-services inflation was slowing, wage pressures were not evident, and inflation expectations remained consistent with the target. AI demand was outpacing supply in chips and semiconductors, while the outlook for elevated energy prices remained highly uncertain. Williams saw little evidence that tariff, geopolitical and AI-related price shocks were spilling significantly into broader, lasting inflation. His continued tightening preference therefore sat alongside specific signs of restraint in the inflation process.

The morning's releases showed a loss of momentum rather than a halt to private-sector growth. S&P Global's November flash composite output PMI fell to 54.6 from October's final 55.9. Services declined to 54.7 from 56.1, below the reported 55.8 forecast, and manufacturing slipped to 54.5 from 54.9 against a 54.6 comparison forecast. Composite and services activity reached four-month lows, while manufacturing was at a three-month low.

Services new business weakened and manufacturing orders were broadly stable. Both sectors continued adding workers. Input-price inflation moderated but remained elevated, and respondents reported more widespread shipping-related disruptions. S&P Global's Chris Williamson estimated that the surveys, conducted November 12-20, were consistent with approximately 3% annualized Q4 GDP growth after actual Q3 growth of 3.4%. Affordability pressures, softer demand and capacity constraints were restraining activity through different channels.

The Chicago Fed National Activity Index supplied a weaker October observation, falling below its historical trend at minus 0.06. Together with the PMI slowdown, it added evidence of moderation to a session in which investors were again allowing for further tightening. Goldman Sachs economist David Mericle argued that high inflation and solid growth left the Fed's course intact for now, while additional tightening in financial conditions connected to weaker risk sentiment or an AI-spending pullback could displace increases next year. Citadel Securities' Frank Flight, in a November 20 note reported Monday, warned that resilient current activity could conceal a deteriorating forward growth outlook, drawing a comparison with late 2018.

Treasury's $69 billion two-year auction encountered solid demand. The high yield was 4.700%, against a 4.703% when-issued yield, and bid-to-cover improved to 2.65 from 2.59. Indirect bidders received about 51.5% of competitive awards, direct bidders 38.1% and primary dealers 10.4%. The 4.625% coupon notes will be issued November 30 and mature November 30, 2028. The small stop-through and stronger coverage showed buyers absorbing the sale during the front-end repricing.

The dollar also recovered, with the dollar index rising 0.51% to 104.337. Gold futures gained 3.39% to $3,634.40 an ounce as metals participated in the rebound from recent selling. UBS strategist Joni Teves said much of gold's liquidation appeared concentrated in futures, while ETF holdings had remained steady. The VIX fell 25.83% to 26.62, although it remained 16.19% above its week-earlier level.

Separately, the Fed's inspector general is reviewing whether Governor Michelle Bowman's June dinner with Bank of America clients breached quiet-period restrictions, according to Bloomberg. Bowman has denied violating the rules. The dinner occurred hours after the June policy meeting; people familiar with the event said her host and accompanying Fed staff reminded attendees that she could not discuss monetary policy, and that her remarks focused on regulation. The review concerns access and communications practices, with no finding announced.

## AI Credit Recovers as Borrowers Seek Capital

Huang's return prompted a substantial repricing of perceived credit risk across the AI financing chain. The CDX investment-grade index spread fell 2.5 basis points to 62.7 basis points, its largest decline since November 4, according to Bloomberg. North America's high-yield credit index, whose price rises as perceived risk declines, gained 0.4 point to 105. European investment-grade and speculative-grade credit gauges also improved.

CoreWeave's 9.625% bonds due in 2032 rose 2.5 cents on the dollar. Invesco's Bixby Stewart described Huang's reinstatement as removing a major source of uncertainty, while Meeder Investment Management's David Klink argued that replacing his willingness to take risks would have been difficult. Their assessments concerned the continuity of Nvidia's role in supporting equipment demand and financing across the ecosystem.

The market's interpretation had changed considerably during Huang's absence. His initial departure had briefly encouraged debt investors who thought Nvidia might limit its extensive financial commitments. By last week, concern about a wider slowdown in AI projects had overtaken that relief. MassMutual's Kelly Kowalski said investors appeared willing to tolerate financing complexity in exchange for greater confidence in Nvidia's business trajectory. Persistence Analytics' Neil Osnato emphasized CoreWeave's ability to turn contractual demand into operational infrastructure and cash flow as the underlying debt-service question.

LQD returned 0.23% including distributions, HYG gained 0.25%, and EMB advanced 0.87%. Those modest bond-fund gains accompanied a much larger recovery in equities. The new confidence in Nvidia's leadership was particularly important for firms dependent on continuing access to external capital, where investment plans stretch beyond installed capacity.

Australia's Firmus Grid is considering a roughly $1.5 billion bond as part of a potential senior and mezzanine debt package of up to about $4 billion, people familiar with the discussions told Bloomberg. That would be substantially smaller than the approximately $7.5 billion package targeted two months earlier. Firmus shelved an IPO last month that had sought as much as $5.5 billion including an overallotment option.

The proposed borrowing would primarily buy Nvidia GB300 chips for an Indonesian data center being developed with DayOne Data Centers. The bond and a separate bank loan under discussion would each run for 69 months and form the senior portion of the package. Indicative bond yield discussions were around 8%, while the loan margin could be about 325 basis points over SOFR. Those are different measures of borrowing cost: the bond figure is a yield, and the loan figure is the premium over a floating reference rate.

The proposed bonds have secured BBB ratings from at least two international rating firms, according to the people, and are expected to rank equally with the bank loan. Morgan Stanley is leading the financing, with banks being invited into the underwriting group. A bond sale could be attempted before year-end, subject to market conditions. Firmus said funding details would be announced at the appropriate time. Its investor documents show a 912-megawatt development pipeline with 46 megawatts built, illustrating the scale of construction still ahead of the planned capacity.

Fresh reporting also described how other AI borrowers are drawing from different funding markets. Anthropic obtained $35 billion through an intricate private-credit arrangement to access Google chips, while Meta used project financing for $12.55 billion of funding for a Texas data center. In SpaceX's already completed chip financing, documents designate some bondholders as a controlling class, a feature associated more closely with asset-backed securities. These structures bring project cash flows, collateral and contractual payment obligations into markets traditionally dominated by direct corporate promises.

JPMorgan Asset Management's Seamus Mac Gorain said heavy corporate AI borrowing, government issuance and central-bank balance-sheet reductions were limiting the scope for sovereign bond rallies. He expected the 10-year Treasury yield to remain between 4.5% and 5.25% until the supply-demand balance changed. In his assessment, a slowdown in hyperscaler issuance was the component most likely to shift, potentially only after 2027. Energy disinflation could support bond prices before the demand for capital had subsided.

Corporate expansion continued through acquisitions as well. CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about $44 billion, one of the cybersecurity industry's largest transactions, while Amazon agreed to pay approximately $7.5 billion for much of Decart AI's assets. ABB agreed to acquire German cooling-systems company Ziehl-Abegg for an equity value of $2.2 billion, expanding its data-center offering. The transactions concern different businesses and funding needs, but collectively show companies continuing to commit capital during a volatile period for technology valuations.

U.S. municipal supply will add a separate infrastructure funding requirement in early December. The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey plans more than $1 billion of bonds for capital spending and refunding, led by Bank of America. About $350 million will be subject to the alternative minimum tax. The debt carries ratings of Aa3 from Moody's and AA- from S&P and Fitch.

The agency's $45 billion capital program is about 22% larger than its predecessor, partly because construction and material costs have risen. Bond documents identify tariffs, long-lead procurement costs and Middle East security uncertainty among the pressures, with possible responses including reduced project scope or deferred spending. A separate $1 billion consolidated-note transaction for the first phase of the Midtown Manhattan bus-terminal replacement is expected to price December 3, led by Morgan Stanley.

## French Fiscal Proposals Meet Uneven Growth

French government bonds outperformed after President Emmanuel Macron raised the possibility of a constitutional rule requiring a multi-year path toward balanced public finances. The French-German 10-year yield spread narrowed 5 basis points to 152 basis points in Bloomberg's Monday account. Macron said his decision would depend partly on borrowing costs and the spread to Germany, particularly if market volatility persisted into January.

The proposal would need a three-fifths majority of lawmakers from the National Assembly and Senate. Finance Minister Roland Lescure argued that a medium-term framework could reduce the annual process of starting budget negotiations afresh. Support for the principle extends beyond Macron's camp, including Marine Le Pen, Bruno Retailleau and former prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal, although their approaches differ. Le Pen has advocated progressive deficit reduction until debt reaches 60% of GDP, while the left opposes the constraint on future democratic choices.

That political breadth helped the proposal's reception, but the intended framework still requires agreement on its design and constitutional approval. Mac Gorain said JPMorgan Asset Management remained away from French debt for now, preferring Italy, and expected the bond market's demand for fiscal restraint eventually to influence policy. The rally therefore accompanied a specific new proposal alongside continued investor caution about implementation.

Fresh business surveys added a less favorable French growth observation. Euro-area composite PMI held at 51.7 in November, below the 51.9 Reuters consensus. Services eased to 51.2 from 51.4 against expectations for 51.8, while manufacturing improved to 52.9 from 52.7, slightly above the 52.8 forecast. Germany's composite reading reached 55.0, its strongest since March 2022. French manufacturing output contracted at its fastest pace since February 2025, increasing the risk of a second quarterly contraction after Q3's decline.

Across the bloc, new orders rose for a fifth month but export-order growth weakened. Manufacturing hiring offset service-sector job losses, business confidence declined for a fourth month, and input and selling-price inflation moderated while remaining elevated. Stable aggregate growth thus contained increasingly different national conditions, with particular significance for France as it seeks a credible budget path.

Germany's automotive industry illustrated a separate weakness beneath its stronger composite survey. IG Metall reported about 340,000 workers participating in walkouts as it sought a 5% wage increase, with additional warning strikes at Mercedes-Benz and Porsche sites. Automotive employment was at its lowest in at least 21 years. Volkswagen is seeking to complete a European factory plan by June 2027, and four German sites have no planned successor vehicle models. Wage negotiations are taking place against pressure from Chinese competition, U.S. tariffs and weaker demand.

Spain's election campaign produced another consequential fiscal proposal. The People's Party pledged income-tax cuts, zero VAT on basic foods while the inflation crisis persists, and tax breaks for first-home buyers if it wins November 29. Economy chief Alberto Nadal said the scale would depend on an independent audit of the public finances and declined to quantify the revenue cost. The party alleged accounting problems, while Spanish and European Commission watchdogs have flagged no irregularities.

The opposition also wants to remove the bank windfall tax that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez plans to extend through 2028 to fund housing. It would seek new deficit and debt targets with the EU, submit a budget by March at the latest, and aim to bring debt clearly below 95% of GDP within four years. Its plans include a EUR300 billion, 15-year infrastructure investment program. The proposals combine lower taxes, additional investment and a debt-reduction objective whose detailed fiscal reconciliation would follow an election victory and audit.

Britain's November PMI showed a moderate slowdown with a different industrial composition. Composite activity fell to 52.3 from 52.9 and services to 52.0 from 52.8. Manufacturing PMI edged down to 52.7 from 52.8, while its output index rose to 54.2 from 53.6 as data-center construction, defense and food production supported demand. Services export orders fell at their fastest pace since February 2021, especially from European customers, and employment contracted again.

S&P Global estimated that the surveys were consistent with 0.6% Q4 GDP growth. Energy, transport, technology and wage costs remained elevated, including Iran-war supplier surcharges, although overall price pressure moderated. Business confidence recovered toward pre-war levels after the recent budget.

BOE Chief Economist Huw Pill argued Monday that action was needed now to preserve inflation credibility. Inflation had been below target in only three of the preceding 62 months, and he warned that accumulated credibility could not be assumed indefinitely. He also said the private sector's resilience to the energy shock might be greater than economic models allowed. Second-round effects remained subdued, but forthcoming wage negotiations mattered with inflation expected to exceed 4% early next year. Bloomberg's account of the remarks put market pricing at an 80% chance of a December increase.

Canada faces a distinct difficulty in obtaining domestic inflation protection. A C$5.25 billion real-return bond matures next month, leaving only seven securities and about C$43 billion outstanding after Ottawa stopped issuance four years ago. The market will represent less than 3% of sovereign debt, compared with about 4.7% in 2022. The finance department said it was not considering restarting issuance, citing objectives including stable, low-cost funding.

Ontario Teachers' chief executive Jo Taylor said the shortage had pushed the pension plan toward U.S. TIPS. CIBC's Ian Pollick argued that the two countries' inflation exposures were diverging, with U.S. core pressure associated with AI investment and Canadian headline inflation driven more by energy. SLC Management warned that diminishing RRB liquidity could raise the cost of inflation-linked products or cause some to disappear. BMO's Earl Davis estimated that rebuilding an efficient market would require five to ten years of consistent issuance, leaving the choice of funding program relevant well beyond the next inflation reading.

## Restructurings and Acquisition Disputes Reorder Claims

Borrower-specific developments continued to determine outcomes away from the broad credit rebound. UBS, Barclays, BNP Paribas and HSBC remain committed to EUR1.2 billion of acquisition financing for Italian food-ingredients maker Irca after CVC sought to withdraw from its purchase from Advent. CVC said forensic due diligence had made the transaction no longer viable. Advent rejected the withdrawal and defended the integrity of the sale process.

The financing commitments remain valid for a period, and people familiar with the matter said the banks could face claims of contractual interference if they tried to alter them. The debt was intended for the high-yield market. Irca bonds traded near 90 cents on the euro Monday after falling as low as 87, compared with around par when investors expected repayment from the acquisition financing.

The purchase agreement has no financing condition. If CVC were required to complete the transaction after the debt commitments expired, it could still need to arrange replacement funding or use equity. Irca has brought earnings forward to November 26, with a bondholder call planned for December 3. The dispute leaves lenders exposed to a signed transaction's legal outcome as well as the price at which acquisition debt could eventually be distributed.

HX Expeditions obtained a standstill from a majority of holders of its super senior secured 2028 bond, allowing debt negotiations without those discussions triggering a default event. The agreement runs through February 15, 2027, and may be extended. The bond, issued at 96 cents on the euro in August, was quoted around 86.5.

The polar-cruise operator has struggled after its separation from Hurtigruten and takeover by lenders in 2025. A new booking system delayed the season, and the company raised additional debt to meet coupon payments. It has flagged a possible Q2 2027 funding gap associated with a ship-lease repayment and refinancing of a cash-management facility. In August, it expected fuel costs to rise 20% from the Q1 run rate. The standstill creates negotiating time against those operating and financing pressures.

Braskem and creditors agreed on the main terms of an out-of-court restructuring, people familiar with the negotiations said. Controlling shareholders Petrobras and IG4 agreed to provide a $1.3 billion capital injection, while creditors agreed to a $3.6 billion debt-to-equity swap. Details remain under discussion, and Braskem intends to seek a court extension of the November 22 deadline to refine the terms.

The agreement supplies amounts and instruments to an earlier framework whose equity commitment had not specified size, structure or timing. Braskem's cash has been depleted by a salt-mine environmental disaster and depressed petrochemical prices. It obtained emergency protection in June and filed for extrajudicial recovery in August. The new shareholder and creditor commitments mark progress toward reworking the balance sheet, with implementation still ahead.

## Brazil's Forecasts Worsen as Sovereign Financing Diverges

Brazil's weekly economist survey showed a further deterioration in the expected policy path. The projected end-2027 Selic rate rose to 13% from 12.75%, while expected inflation increased to 5.12% from 5%, the second consecutive weekly upward revision in both forecasts. The currency weakened beyond 6 reais per dollar Monday, adding import-price pressure to concern over fiscal policy under President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's next term.

The government separately revised its own forecasts toward weaker growth and higher inflation. It now expects 2027 growth of 1.8%, down from 2.3%, and inflation of 4.5%, up from 3.8%. For 2026, growth was cut to 1.9% from 2.0% and inflation raised to 5.3% from 4.9%. Those assumptions will inform the final 2026 fiscal assessment and amendments to the 2027 budget. The ministry cited restrictive borrowing costs, a smaller agricultural contribution and weaker statistical carryover in explaining the growth revision.

Finance Minister Durigan said the government would seek a primary surplus of 1.5%-2.0% of GDP by the end of Lula's next term and identified restoration of investment-grade sovereign status as an objective. The existing budget-guidelines bill envisaged a surplus of up to 1.5% in 2030. He endorsed the 3% inflation target and said accelerated economic measures in 2027 should not imply faster government spending. Outstanding central-bank and regulatory appointments could be resolved within two weeks, he said.

Central-bank Governor Gabriel Galipolo focused on expenditure mechanics. Spending rising faster than GDP in an economy near full employment could generate inflation, he said, while acknowledging the purchasing-power benefits of higher minimum wages. The fiscal framework permits real spending growth equal to 70% of revenue growth, subject to a 0.6% floor and 2.5% ceiling. Galipolo highlighted feedback from revenue-linked expenditure and said fiscal adjustments could preserve social programs while improving coordination with monetary policy. His remarks supplied a more specific account of the inflation constraint than the exchange rate alone.

Senegal delivered a concrete debt-service payment while official financing remained dependent on a contested budget process. The Treasury said it paid the scheduled coupon on its 2033 dollar bonds within the deadline; $31.25 million was due Monday. Approval of a proposed $2.2 billion IMF program depends partly on revised 2026 and 2027 budgets that curb expenditure.

President Bassirou Diomaye Faye enacted the revised 2026 plan by decree after parliament blocked it, and lawmakers also rejected the first part of the 2027 budget last week. The majority Pastef party has resisted spending restraint and external-debt restructuring, and expelled Faye and 31 other members on November 17. Oxford Economics' Francois Conradie said Faye could dissolve parliament from December 2, creating the possibility of a snap election.

EBRD President Odile Renaud-Basso said clarity on Senegal's macroeconomic position and progress on debt would be crucial to the institution's private-sector investment decisions. Elsewhere in West Africa, the lender announced a EUR250 million package with Ivory Coast's SGCI, including a EUR100 million risk-sharing facility and EUR50 million trade line. EBRD has now signed close to EUR500 million of investment in Ivory Coast. The contrasting developments show official support advancing through different country and institutional conditions.

Nigeria's currency faced a renewed political and funding test. The naira weakened to 1,403.50 per dollar Monday before paring losses after central-bank intervention, according to traders, and was down 3.6% in November. Chapel Hill Denham analyst Nabila Mohammed said investors were withdrawing funds as open-market-operation bills matured, with foreign portfolio investors recording $1.02 billion of net outflows in the quarter to date.

President Bola Tinubu remains the front-runner in January's election, but public anger over living costs and opposition suggestions of restoring fuel subsidies have made the durability of reforms an investment concern. Standard Chartered's Samir Gadio said some investors had become more reluctant to increase exposure to emerging markets facing elections after Brazil's unexpected result.

The pressure follows substantial earlier bond gains. Aktia's Mikko Kuisma said Nigerian local bonds had returned 21% this year against 3.1% for Bloomberg's local-bond index. His fund, which added Nigeria and Kazakhstan while reducing oil-importer exposure, returned 6% over the past year and outperformed 99% of peers. Foreign ownership of Kazakhstan's local bonds reached a record ahead of GBI-EM inclusion, while the tenge gained 12% this year. These performance comparisons describe the accumulated benefits of earlier trades alongside Nigeria's current currency outflow.

India's November flash surveys showed stronger factories and softer services. Manufacturing PMI rose to a nine-month high of 56.0 from 54.7, services eased to 55.3 from 55.8, and the composite edged up to 56.3 from 56.2. Factory employment grew at its fastest pace in seven months, while services employment contracted for the first time in nearly a year. Input-cost inflation was relatively mild but selling prices accelerated, with stronger manufacturing production and orders driving the aggregate improvement.

RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said the country's redesigned GDP and inflation series should improve forecasting and policy calibration. The smaller food weight in CPI and more detailed geographic and product coverage would help identify the breadth of price changes, she said. Her intervention concerned how the central bank measures a fast-growing economy as it prepares its next decision, adding a statistical-policy dimension to the fresh sectoral divergence.

Hungary's central bank signaled caution about easing after the forint's recent volatility. Deputy Governor Zoltan Kurali called the swings excessive and emphasized joint consideration of domestic and international conditions. The currency rose 1.3% against the euro as his remarks coincided with Huang's reinstatement and the response to Moody's improved outlook. Kurali said the easing cycle had ended in September, qualifying last week's opening to possible December cuts when new inflation forecasts arrive.

Israel's central bank delivered the expected hold at 3.25%, its second consecutive unchanged decision, supported by 12 of 14 surveyed economists. October inflation slowed to 1.1% annually from 1.6%, close to the bottom of the 1%-3% target, but the shekel had weakened nearly 8% since the October 21 meeting. Government formation remains unresolved after October 27's inconclusive election, and renewed conflict with Iran remains a risk. The bank expects inflation to exceed 2% during the coming year. Q3 growth was 8% annualized, or 4% excluding Israeli companies' overseas production, leaving currency, political and demand considerations alongside the low current inflation rate.

## Forward Market Significance

Tuesday, November 24 brings ADP's four-week-average employment observation at 8:15 a.m. Eastern, followed at 10 a.m. by Conference Board consumer confidence and the Richmond Fed manufacturing index. Confidence is expected to improve to 92.4 from 91.7, and Richmond's index to rise to 2 from minus 2. The releases will add household and regional detail after the national PMI slowdown, with continued hiring and affordability pressures central to the balance between growth and restraint.

Wednesday's 8:30 a.m. releases concentrate the larger U.S. policy test. Core PCE prices are expected to rise 0.3% month on month, matching the previous reading, while Bloomberg-surveyed economists expect headline PCE inflation of 3.8% annually and real personal spending growth of 0.1%. The annualized GDP estimate is expected at 3.4%, and durable-goods orders are forecast to increase 0.4% after 1.8%. Williams' gradual return-to-target forecast leaves the persistence and breadth of price pressure particularly important as December 8-9 approaches.

Treasury's five-year auction is scheduled for Tuesday at 1 p.m. Eastern, following Monday's well-covered two-year sale. Demand will be tested at a maturity that gave back part of its rally as December tightening expectations recovered. The U.S. bond market closes Thursday for Thanksgiving and has a shortened Friday session, concentrating activity and economic information into fewer trading hours.

In corporate credit, Irca's November 26 earnings and December 3 investor call will provide the next company disclosures while the acquisition dispute leaves financing commitments unresolved. Braskem's remaining restructuring terms and court extension, and Firmus' prospective debt package, are separate execution questions with different shareholder, lender and market conditions.

Spain's November 29 election will determine whether the proposed tax cuts, fiscal audit and investment program move toward government policy. France's constitutional proposal depends on agreement across political camps, with Macron linking his decision partly to market conditions into January. Senegal's budget dispute has a nearer constitutional milestone on December 2, when a parliamentary dissolution becomes possible. Each presents a different route from political intent to an executable fiscal framework.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries flatten as Huang's return restores tightening bets and falling oil supports long bonds
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Short-dated Treasuries surrendered part of their haven rally after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, restoring confidence in AI investment and expectations of a December Fed increase. The 2-year yield rose 4.69 basis points to 4.6938%, while the 10-year edged down 0.01 basis point to 4.9437% and the 30-year fell 2.3 basis points to 5.3068%. The 2- to 10-year spread narrowed 4.7 basis points to 24.99 basis points.

Falling oil supported longer bonds by reducing inflation compensation. The 10-year breakeven fell 2.4 basis points to 2.1428%, offsetting a 2.39-basis-point rise in the real yield to 2.8009%. Lower energy inflation thus coexisted with a higher inflation-adjusted financing cost. John Williams maintained the case for further inflation restraint as November's U.S. composite PMI slowed to 54.6 from 55.9, with hiring continuing and costs still elevated.

Technology bonds rebounded as Huang's return eased uncertainty about Nvidia's support for the AI financing chain. The S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.86%, a much larger recovery than the gains in corporate bond funds. Borrowers still face substantial capital needs: Firmus Grid is considering a roughly $1.5 billion bond within a potential debt package of up to about $4 billion. Wednesday's inflation, spending and growth releases will test the restored expectations of monetary restraint.

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 債市主線

Nvidia董事會讓黃仁勳復職，重振市場對人工智慧投資的信心，也使12月聯準會升息的預期回升，短天期美國公債因而回吐部分避險漲幅。油價下跌則支撐長天期公債，殖利率曲線明顯趨平：2年期殖利率上升4.69個基點至4.6938%，10年期大致持平於4.9437%，30年期下降2.3個基點至5.3068%。

風險偏好回升也帶動企業債，科技債反彈，信用保護成本下降。不過，相較標普500指數大漲4.73%、那斯達克100指數上漲6.86%，美國公債的反應相當有限。能源價格下跌壓低通膨補償，實質殖利率卻上升；油價衝擊緩解與投資融資成本的走向，仍有重要差別。

紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams仍主張進一步採取行動抑制通膨。美國最新企業調查則顯示，擴張速度放慢，但企業持續增聘人手，成本也居高不下。市場重新肯定AI產業領導層，貨幣政策的緊縮程度並未隨之同幅退讓。

## 美國景氣放緩，公債曲線趨平

美國現貨市場開盤前，股指期貨已自前一週科技股重挫後反彈。隨後，Nvidia董事會在聽取美國政府高層意見後，決定讓黃仁勳立即復職，總統川普也對此表示支持。Nvidia股價上漲約31%，半導體類股收高14.03%，大幅扭轉產業估值先前承受的短期壓力。

Floodlines Research策略師Anna Wu指出，AI股遭拋售時流入美國公債的避險需求，已有一部分撤出。交易員重新建立緊縮預期，帶動對政策敏感的殖利率上升。Bloomberg週一的利率報導指出，期貨市場再次完全反映聯準會12月升息25個基點的預期，升息50個基點的預期則相當有限。上週五避險行情一度排除的部分政策緊縮，如今重新進入市場定價。

越往長天期，這波調整越小。5年期殖利率上升2.15個基點至4.7618%，10年期僅下降0.01個基點；2年與10年期利差收窄4.7個基點至24.99個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄6.99個基點至61.3個基點。即使短天期公債價格回跌，2年期殖利率仍比11月16日低13.56個基點，10年期則低18.74個基點，週一僅扭轉近期公債漲勢的一部分。

油價是影響曲線的另一項主要因素。WTI期貨下跌3.79%至每桶$80.25，Brent下跌3.49%至$89.34，兩者本月跌幅均達約20%。Bloomberg的利率報導將原油下跌與通膨補償降低、長天期公債獲得支撐連結起來，歐洲公債也受惠。美國公債期貨交易異常熱絡，截至紐約下午3時，多數合約成交量至少高於20日均量15%。

10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2.4個基點至2.1428%，幾乎完全抵銷實質殖利率上升2.39個基點至2.8009%的影響。從本月變化來看，兩者的分歧更明顯：損益兩平通膨率下降21.02個基點，實質殖利率上升15.94個基點。因此，名目殖利率雖較月初下降5.08個基點，經通膨調整後的融資成本仍然升高。

Williams週一的談話，為這波重新定價提供了最新政策看法。他表示，經濟依然強勁、通膨仍過高，需要持續採取行動，讓通膨可持續地回到2%目標。他預測2026年與2027年實質經濟成長率均約2.75%，失業率則由4.1%降至明年接近4%；通膨率今年為3.5%，明年略高於2%，2028年回到目標。通膨風險仍偏向上行，12月8日至9日的政策決定將取決於後續數據。

他也區分了特定產業漲價與更廣泛、持續性的通膨。關稅影響大致消退，住宅服務通膨放緩，未見明顯薪資壓力，通膨預期仍與目標一致。晶片與半導體的AI需求超過供給，能源價格持續偏高的前景則高度不確定。Williams認為，關稅、地緣政治與AI相關價格衝擊大幅擴散為廣泛、持久通膨的跡象有限。他傾向繼續緊縮，同時也承認通膨形成過程已有若干具體抑制因素。

當日上午發布的數據顯示，民間經濟仍在成長，但動能轉弱。S&P Global的11月綜合產出PMI初值，由10月終值55.9降至54.6；服務業由56.1降至54.7，低於報導所列的55.8預測；製造業由54.9降至54.5，也略低於54.6的比較預測值。綜合與服務業活動均降至四個月低點，製造業則為三個月低點。

服務業新業務減弱，製造業訂單大致持平，兩個產業仍持續增聘員工。投入價格通膨雖然放緩，水準依舊偏高，受訪企業也表示，航運相關干擾更為普遍。S&P Global的Chris Williamson估計，11月12日至20日進行的調查，與第四季GDP年化成長約3%相符，低於第三季實際成長3.4%。負擔能力壓力、需求轉弱與產能限制，正透過不同管道抑制活動。

芝加哥聯準銀行全國活動指數則提供了更疲弱的10月觀察值，降至-0.06，低於歷史趨勢。這項數據與PMI放緩共同顯示景氣降溫，但投資人當日仍重新納入進一步緊縮的可能。高盛經濟學家David Mericle認為，高通膨與穩健成長使聯準會目前的政策路徑維持不變；若風險情緒轉差或AI支出縮減，使金融情勢進一步收緊，可能取代明年的升息。Citadel Securities的Frank Flight在11月20日、於週一被報導的研究中，將情況與2018年底相比，提醒當前活動的韌性可能掩蓋未來成長前景惡化。

美國財政部標售$690億2年期公債，需求穩健。得標最高殖利率為4.700%，低於發行前交易殖利率4.703%；投標倍數由2.59升至2.65。間接投標人取得約51.5%的競標配售額，直接投標人占38.1%，初級交易商占10.4%。這批票息4.625%的債券將於11月30日發行，2028年11月30日到期。得標殖利率略低於發行前交易水準，加上投標倍數提高，顯示短端重新定價之際，買盤仍能消化供給。

美元同步回升，美元指數上漲0.51%至104.337。金屬也加入近期賣壓後的反彈，黃金期貨上漲3.39%至每盎司$3,634.40。瑞銀策略師Joni Teves表示，黃金賣出平倉似乎主要集中在期貨，ETF持有量則保持穩定。VIX下跌25.83%至26.62，但仍比一週前高16.19%。

另據Bloomberg報導，聯準會監察長正檢視理事Michelle Bowman於6月與美國銀行客戶共進晚餐，是否違反政策靜默期規定。Bowman否認違規。晚餐在6月政策會議結束數小時後舉行；知情人士表示，作東者與陪同的聯準會人員都曾提醒與會者，她不能討論貨幣政策，談話內容集中在監管。這項檢視涉及接觸官員與溝通的作法，目前尚未公布調查結論。

## AI信用風險緩解，企業持續籌資

黃仁勳回任，促使市場大幅重估AI融資鏈的信用風險。據Bloomberg報導，CDX投資級指數利差下降2.5個基點至62.7個基點，為11月4日以來最大單日降幅。北美高收益信用指數上漲0.4點至105；該指數價格上升代表市場感知風險下降。歐洲投資級與投機級信用指標也有所改善。

CoreWeave的2032年到期、票息9.625%債券，每$1面額價格上漲2.5美分。Invesco的Bixby Stewart認為，黃仁勳復職排除了一項重大不確定性；Meeder Investment Management的David Klink則表示，很難找到能取代他、同樣願意承擔風險的人選。兩人的看法都涉及Nvidia能否持續在整個生態系中支撐設備需求與融資。

黃仁勳離任期間，市場解讀已明顯轉變。他最初離職時，一些債券投資人認為Nvidia可能縮減大規模財務承諾，一度因此感到寬慰；到了上週，對AI專案可能普遍放緩的擔憂已蓋過這種情緒。MassMutual的Kelly Kowalski表示，投資人似乎願意接受複雜的融資關係，換取對Nvidia業務走向更大的信心。Persistence Analytics的Neil Osnato則強調，CoreWeave能否把合約需求轉化為運作中的基礎設施與現金流，才是償債能力的根本問題。

計入配息後，LQD報酬為0.23%，HYG上漲0.25%，EMB上漲0.87%，債券基金漲幅遠小於股票。對投資計畫超出已建置產能、必須持續向外部取得資本的公司而言，市場重新肯定Nvidia領導層尤其重要。

知情人士向Bloomberg表示，澳洲Firmus Grid正考慮發行約$15億債券，納入一項可能高達約$40億的優先順位及夾層債務融資方案，規模顯著小於兩個月前約$75億的目標。公司上月已擱置一項原擬連同超額配售選擇權籌集至多$55億的IPO。

這筆擬議借款主要用於購買Nvidia GB300晶片，供公司與DayOne Data Centers在印尼共同開發的資料中心使用。正在洽談的債券與另一筆銀行貸款，期限均為69個月，構成方案中的優先順位部分。債券殖利率初步討論約為8%，貸款則可能按浮動參考利率SOFR加碼約325個基點計息。

知情人士表示，擬發行債券已取得至少兩家國際信評機構的BBB評等，預計與銀行貸款具有同等清償順位。摩根士丹利主導融資，正邀請銀行加入承銷團；若市場條件許可，可能在年底前嘗試發債。Firmus表示，將於適當時機公布融資細節。其投資人文件顯示，開發中的專案規模合計912百萬瓦，已建成46百萬瓦，可見計畫產能仍有相當大的建設工作待完成。

最新報導也呈現其他AI借款人如何利用不同融資市場。Anthropic透過複雜的私人信貸安排取得$350億，以使用Google晶片；Meta則以專案融資為德州一座資料中心籌得$125.5億。SpaceX已完成的晶片融資中，文件將部分債券持有人指定為具有控制權的類別，這種設計更常見於資產擔保證券。這些結構把專案現金流、擔保品與合約付款義務，帶進過去以企業直接償付承諾為主的市場。

摩根資產管理的Seamus Mac Gorain認為，企業大量為AI舉債、政府發債與央行縮表，正限制主權債券上漲空間。他預期，在供需平衡改變前，10年期美國公債殖利率將維持在4.5%至5.25%。他認為，最可能改變的是超大型雲端業者發債放緩，但可能要到2027年之後才會發生。能源帶來的通膨降溫，可以在資本需求尚未減弱前先支撐債券價格。

企業也持續透過併購擴張。CrowdStrike同意以約$440億收購Zscaler，成為資安產業規模最大的交易之一；Amazon同意支付約$75億，購買Decart AI的大部分資產。ABB則同意以$22億股權價值收購德國冷卻系統公司Ziehl-Abegg，擴充資料中心產品與服務。這些交易涉及不同業務與融資需求，合計顯示科技估值波動之際，企業仍繼續投入資本。

12月初，美國地方政府債市場將有另一批基礎設施融資需求。紐約與紐澤西港務局計畫發行逾$10億債券，用於資本支出與借新還舊，由美國銀行主導，其中約$3.5億適用替代性最低稅負。債券獲穆迪Aa3、標普與惠譽AA-評等。

港務局的$450億資本計畫比上一期大約增加22%，部分原因是營建與材料成本上升。債券文件將關稅、長交期採購成本及中東安全情勢不明列為壓力，可能透過縮小工程範圍或延後支出因應。另外一筆$10億綜合票據交易，將用於曼哈頓中城巴士總站改建的第一階段，預計12月3日定價，由摩根士丹利主導。

## 法國推財政規則，歐洲成長分化

法國總統馬克宏提出，可能透過憲法規則，要求政府採取多年期路徑邁向公共財政平衡，帶動法國公債表現優於同業。Bloomberg週一報導，法德10年期公債利差收窄5個基點至152個基點。馬克宏表示，他的決定將部分取決於借款成本與對德國利差，尤其若市場波動延續至1月。

這項提案須取得國民議會與參議院合計五分之三議員支持。財長Roland Lescure認為，中期架構可減少每年重新從頭協商預算的情況。支持這項原則者不限於馬克宏陣營，還包括Marine Le Pen、Bruno Retailleau，以及前總理Edouard Philippe與Gabriel Attal，但各方作法不同。Le Pen主張逐步減少赤字，直到債務降至GDP的60%；左派則反對限制未來民主選擇。

跨陣營支持有助於市場接受這項提案，但具體設計仍須取得共識並完成修憲程序。Mac Gorain表示，摩根資產管理目前仍避開法國債券，偏好義大利，並預期債市對財政節制的要求最終將影響政策。法債上漲反映這項具體新提議，投資人對落實情況仍抱持審慎態度。

最新企業調查則顯示，法國成長情況較不樂觀。歐元區11月綜合PMI持平於51.7，低於路透調查預估的51.9；服務業由51.4降至51.2，低於51.8的預期；製造業由52.7升至52.9，略高於52.8的預測。德國綜合指數達55.0，為2022年3月以來最高；法國製造業產出卻以2025年2月以來最快速度萎縮，增加了第三季衰退後、連續第二季萎縮的風險。

歐元區新訂單連續第五個月增加，但出口訂單成長減弱。製造業增聘人員抵銷了服務業裁員，企業信心則連續第四個月下降。投入與銷售價格通膨均放緩，水準仍偏高。整體成長穩定之下，各國情況日益分歧，對正在尋求可信預算路徑的法國尤其重要。

德國綜合調查走強，汽車業卻呈現另一項弱點。德國金屬工業工會表示，約34萬名勞工參與停工，要求加薪5%，Mercedes-Benz與Porsche廠區也有進一步警告性罷工。汽車業就業降至至少21年來最低。Volkswagen正力求在2027年6月前完成歐洲工廠計畫，德國有四座廠區尚未規畫後續車款。薪資協商同時面臨中國競爭、美國關稅與需求轉弱的壓力。

西班牙選戰帶來另一項重要財政提案。人民黨承諾，若在11月29日勝選，將調降所得稅，並在通膨危機持續期間，將基本食品增值稅降為零，同時提供首購族稅賦優惠。其經濟事務負責人Alberto Nadal表示，規模將取決於對公共財政的獨立審計，未量化稅收損失。人民黨指控帳目有問題，但西班牙與歐盟執委會監督機構均未指出異常。

反對黨也希望取消銀行暴利稅；總理Pedro Sanchez則計畫將這項稅延長至2028年，為住宅政策提供資金。人民黨將尋求與歐盟議定新的赤字及債務目標，最遲3月提交預算，並力求在四年內，讓債務明顯降至GDP的95%以下。計畫另包括一項為期15年、規模€3,000億的基礎設施投資方案。減稅、增加投資與降債目標如何在財政上具體整合，仍待勝選與審計後釐清。

英國11月PMI顯示景氣溫和放緩，產業結構則有所不同。綜合指數由52.9降至52.3，服務業由52.8降至52.0；製造業PMI由52.8微降至52.7，但產出指數由53.6升至54.2，資料中心建設、國防與食品生產支撐需求。服務業出口訂單降幅為2021年2月以來最大，尤其是來自歐洲客戶的訂單，就業也再度萎縮。

S&P Global估計，調查與第四季GDP成長0.6%相符。整體價格壓力雖然減輕，能源、運輸、科技與薪資成本仍偏高，包括供應商因伊朗戰爭加收的費用。近期預算公布後，企業信心回升至接近戰前水準。

英格蘭銀行首席經濟學家Huw Pill週一主張，現在就必須採取行動，以維護抑制通膨的公信力。過去62個月中，通膨只有三個月低於目標；他提醒，不能假設累積的公信力能無限期維持。他也認為，民間部門抵禦能源衝擊的韌性，可能高於經濟模型所估。第二輪效應仍有限，但通膨預計明年初將超過4%，使接下來的薪資協商格外重要。Bloomberg報導這段談話時指出，市場定價顯示12月升息機率為80%。

加拿大則面臨取得本國通膨保障的困難。一筆C$52.5億實質報酬債券將於下月到期；自渥太華四年前停止發行後，市場將只剩七檔債券，流通餘額約C$430億，占主權債務比重將低於3%，2022年則約為4.7%。財政部表示，目前不考慮恢復發行，理由包括維持穩定、低成本融資等目標。

安大略省教師退休金計畫執行長Jo Taylor表示，供給短缺已促使該退休基金轉向美國抗通膨公債（TIPS）。CIBC的Ian Pollick指出，兩國通膨曝險正在分化：美國核心通膨壓力與AI投資有關，加拿大整體通膨則更多由能源帶動。SLC Management警告，實質報酬債券（RRB）流動性減弱，可能提高抗通膨商品成本，或使部分商品消失。BMO的Earl Davis估計，必須持續發債五至十年，才能重建有效率的市場；因此，發債安排的影響遠超過下一次通膨數據。

## 重整與併購爭議牽動債權安排

整體信用市場反彈之外，個別借款人的進展仍左右投資結果。CVC試圖退出向Advent收購義大利食品原料商Irca的交易，但瑞銀、巴克萊、法國巴黎銀行與滙豐，仍承諾提供€12億收購融資。CVC表示，鑑識性盡職調查使交易不再可行；Advent拒絕接受撤回，並維護出售程序的完整性。

融資承諾在一段期間內仍然有效。知情人士表示，若銀行試圖修改承諾，可能面臨干預契約的求償。這批債務原擬在高收益債市場銷售。Irca債券週一約在每€1面額90歐分交易，先前一度跌至87歐分；投資人原本預期收購融資將用於償還債券時，價格約為面額。

收購協議不以取得融資為成交前提。因此，若CVC在債務承諾到期後仍被要求完成交易，可能必須另覓融資或動用股權資金。Irca已將財報提前至11月26日公布，並計畫12月3日舉行債券持有人電話會議。貸款銀行既須面對已簽約交易的法律結果，也承擔收購債務最終能以何種價格分銷的風險。

HX Expeditions取得其2028年到期、最高優先順位擔保債券多數持有人的暫緩行使權利協議，可進行債務協商，而不因協商本身觸發違約事件。協議效期至2027年2月15日，並可延長。這批債券8月以每€1面額96歐分發行，目前報價約86.5歐分。

這家極地郵輪業者自與Hurtigruten分拆、並於2025年由貸款人接手後，營運一直不順。新訂位系統延誤營運季，公司也曾增借債務以支付票息。公司已指出，船舶租賃款償付及現金管理融資工具再融資，可能使2027年第二季出現資金缺口；8月時則預期，燃料成本將比第一季的支出水準增加20%。暫緩行使權利協議讓公司有時間處理這些營運與融資壓力。

知情人士表示，Braskem與債權人已就庭外重整的主要條款達成協議。控股股東Petrobras與IG4同意注資$13億，債權人則同意進行$36億債轉股。細節仍在討論，Braskem計畫向法院申請延長11月22日的期限，以進一步敲定條款。

先前架構尚未說明股權投入的規模、結構與時程，如今協議已提供金額與工具。鹽礦環境災難及石化產品價格低迷，持續消耗Braskem現金；公司6月取得緊急保護，8月申請庭外重整。股東與債權人的新承諾，代表資產負債表重整有所進展，後續仍待落實。

## 巴西預測惡化，各國主權融資分歧

巴西每週經濟學家調查顯示，預期政策路徑進一步惡化。2027年底Selic政策利率預測由12.75%升至13%，通膨預測由5%升至5.12%，兩項均連續第二週上修。週一雷亞爾貶破每美元兌6雷亞爾，增加進口價格壓力，也使市場對總統魯拉下個任期財政政策的疑慮升高。

政府本身也另行下修成長、上修通膨預測：2027年經濟成長由2.3%降至1.8%，通膨由3.8%升至4.5%；2026年成長由2.0%降至1.9%，通膨由4.9%升至5.3%。這些假設將用於2026年最終財政評估與2027年預算修正。財政部解釋，借款成本對經濟的抑制、農業貢獻縮小及較弱的經濟成長統計翹尾效應，是下修成長的原因。

財長Durigan表示，政府將力求在魯拉下個任期結束前，達成GDP的1.5%至2.0%初級財政盈餘，並以恢復主權投資級評等為目標。現有預算指導法案設定2030年盈餘最高為1.5%。他支持3%的通膨目標，並表示2027年加快推動經濟措施，不應意味政府支出加速；尚待完成的央行與監管人事任命，可能在兩週內解決。

央行總裁Gabriel Galipolo則聚焦支出機制。他表示，在接近充分就業的經濟中，支出成長快於GDP可能推升通膨，同時也肯定最低工資提高對購買力的幫助。財政架構容許實質支出成長相當於收入成長的70%，下限0.6%、上限2.5%。Galipolo強調支出與收入連動所帶來的回饋，並表示財政調整可以在維持社會計畫的同時，改善與貨幣政策的協調。相較僅觀察匯率，他的說法更具體交代了通膨對政策的限制。

塞內加爾完成一筆實際償債付款，但官方融資仍取決於充滿爭議的預算程序。財政部表示，已在期限內支付2033年到期美元債的當期票息，週一應付金額為$3,125萬。一項擬議中的$22億國際貨幣基金（IMF）計畫能否獲批，部分取決於2026年與2027年修訂預算是否抑制支出。

國會阻擋修訂後的2026年預算後，總統Bassirou Diomaye Faye以命令使其生效；議員上週也否決2027年預算的第一部分。掌握多數席次的Pastef黨反對支出節制與外債重整，並於11月17日開除Faye及其他31名成員。Oxford Economics的Francois Conradie表示，Faye可自12月2日起解散國會，可能因此提前舉行選舉。

歐洲復興開發銀行（EBRD）總裁Odile Renaud-Basso表示，塞內加爾總體經濟情況能否釐清，以及債務處理進展，將是該行決定民間部門投資的關鍵。在西非其他地方，EBRD宣布與象牙海岸SGCI合作推出€2.5億方案，包括€1億風險分攤工具及€5,000萬貿易融資額度。EBRD迄今在象牙海岸簽署的投資已接近€5億。這些不同進展顯示，官方支持會隨各國情況與機構條件，以不同方式推進。

奈及利亞貨幣再次面臨政治與資金考驗。交易員表示，奈拉週一一度貶至每美元兌1,403.50奈拉，央行干預後收斂跌幅，11月以來仍下跌3.6%。Chapel Hill Denham分析師Nabila Mohammed指出，公開市場操作票券到期後，投資人正在撤出資金；外國證券投資人本季迄今淨流出$10.2億。

總統Bola Tinubu仍是1月大選最被看好的候選人，但民眾對生活成本不滿，加上反對派提出恢復燃料補貼，使改革能否持續成為投資疑慮。渣打的Samir Gadio表示，巴西選舉出現意外結果後，一些投資人對增加面臨選舉的新興市場曝險更為猶豫。

當前壓力出現在先前債券已大幅上漲之後。Aktia的Mikko Kuisma表示，奈及利亞本幣債今年報酬達21%，Bloomberg本幣債指數則為3.1%。他的基金增加奈及利亞與哈薩克部位、降低石油進口國曝險，過去一年報酬6%，表現優於99%的同業。哈薩克即將納入GBI-EM指數，外資持有其本幣債券的規模已創紀錄，堅戈今年上漲12%。這些績效比較呈現先前交易累積的收益，同時奈及利亞目前正面臨匯市資金外流。

印度11月初值調查顯示，製造業增強、服務業轉弱。製造業PMI由54.7升至56.0，為九個月高點；服務業由55.8降至55.3，綜合指數則由56.2微升至56.3。工廠就業以七個月來最快速度增加，服務業就業則近一年來首次萎縮。投入成本通膨相對溫和，但銷售價格加速上漲；製造業生產與訂單走強，帶動整體改善。

印度央行副總裁Poonam Gupta表示，重新設計的GDP與通膨數列，應有助於改善預測與政策調整。她指出，CPI中的食品權重降低，加上更細緻的地理與商品涵蓋範圍，有助於辨別價格變化的廣度。央行準備下一次政策決策之際，她的談話聚焦如何衡量快速成長的經濟，為最新產業分化增添了統計與政策層面的考量。

匈牙利央行在福林近期波動後，對寬鬆政策釋出審慎訊號。副總裁Zoltan Kurali認為波動過度，強調須同時考量國內外情勢。他發言之際，適逢黃仁勳回任與市場回應穆迪調升展望，福林兌歐元上漲1.3%。Kurali表示，降息循環已在9月結束，使上週保留的12月降息可能性進一步受限；12月將有新的通膨預測。

以色列央行如預期維持政策利率3.25%，連續第二次按兵不動，受訪14位經濟學家中有12位預期此結果。10月年通膨率由1.6%降至1.1%，接近1%至3%目標區間下緣，但謝克爾自10月21日會議以來已貶值近8%。10月27日選舉未有明確結果後，組閣仍懸而未決，與伊朗衝突再起也是風險。央行預期未來一年通膨將超過2%。第三季經濟年化成長8%，若排除以色列企業的海外生產則為4%；因此，當前低通膨之外，匯率、政治與需求也是政策考量。

## 後續市場焦點

11月24日週二，美東時間上午8時15分將公布ADP四週平均就業數據，上午10時接著公布經濟諮商理事會消費者信心與里奇蒙聯準銀行製造業指數。消費者信心預估由91.7升至92.4，里奇蒙指數由-2升至2。全國PMI放緩後，這些數據將補充家庭與區域情況；就業持續增加與負擔能力壓力，仍是衡量成長及政策抑制效果的關鍵。

週三上午8時30分的密集數據，是美國政策更重要的考驗。核心PCE物價預計月增0.3%，與前值相同；Bloomberg調查經濟學家預期，整體PCE通膨年增3.8%，實質個人支出成長0.1%。GDP年化成長率估計為3.4%，耐久財訂單則預估成長0.4%，低於前次的1.8%。Williams預測通膨將逐步回到目標，隨著12月8日至9日會議接近，價格壓力的持續性與廣度格外重要。

美國財政部將於週二美東時間下午1時標售5年期公債，接續週一需求充足的2年期標售。12月緊縮預期回升，使5年期回吐部分先前漲幅，這次標售將檢驗該期限的需求。美國債市週四因感恩節休市，週五縮短交易，經濟資訊與交易活動將集中於較少的交易時段。

企業信用方面，Irca將於11月26日公布財報、12月3日舉行投資人電話會議，提供下一批公司資訊，而併購爭議中的融資承諾仍未解決。Braskem剩餘重整條款與法院展延，以及Firmus擬議債務方案，各有不同的股東、貸款人與市場條件，須分別觀察能否落實。

西班牙11月29日大選，將決定擬議減稅、財政審計與投資計畫能否邁向政府政策。法國修憲提案取決於政治陣營間的共識，馬克宏的決定也部分繫於延續至1月的市場情況。塞內加爾預算爭議則有更近的憲政時點：12月2日起可解散國會。各國從政治意向走向可落實財政架構的途徑，並不相同。

overall_summary.headline: 黃仁勳回任帶動升息預期，油價下跌支撐長債，美債曲線趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Nvidia讓黃仁勳復職，重振AI投資信心，也使12月聯準會升息預期回升，短天期美國公債回吐部分避險漲幅。2年期殖利率上升4.69個基點至4.6938%，10年期微降0.01個基點至4.9437%，30年期下降2.3個基點至5.3068%；2年與10年期利差收窄4.7個基點至24.99個基點。

油價下跌壓低通膨補償，支撐長天期債券。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2.4個基點至2.1428%，抵銷實質殖利率上升2.39個基點至2.8009%的影響。能源通膨降低，經通膨調整後的融資成本仍升高。John Williams繼續主張加強抑制通膨；美國11月綜合PMI由55.9降至54.6，企業仍持續增聘人手，成本也居高不下。

黃仁勳回任，降低了市場對Nvidia能否繼續支撐AI融資鏈的疑慮，帶動科技債反彈。標普500指數上漲4.73%，那斯達克100指數上漲6.86%，漲勢遠大於企業債基金。借款人仍有龐大資本需求：Firmus Grid正考慮發行約$15億債券，納入可能高達約$40億的債務方案。週三的通膨、支出與成長數據，將檢驗重新升高的貨幣緊縮預期。
overall_summary.summary: 黃仁勳重返Nvidia，提振AI信用市場並推升對政策敏感的殖利率；油價下跌壓低通膨補償，抵銷實質殖利率上升的影響，使10年期名目殖利率大致持平。

section_summaries.summary: 黃仁勳回任Nvidia，重振AI投資信心與企業信用市場，使短天期美國公債的部分避險需求退潮。油價下跌支撐長端，在實質殖利率上升之際壓低通膨補償。殖利率曲線趨平，反映風險偏好回升、貨幣政策仍具抑制性；美國調查則顯示擴張放慢，但就業持續增加、成本仍高。

section_summaries.market_read: 本月10年期名目殖利率下降5.08個基點，實質殖利率卻上升15.94個基點，實質融資成本因而提高。
section_summaries.section_title: 美國景氣放緩，公債曲線趨平
section_summaries.summary: 黃仁勳回任使12月緊縮預期回升，帶動美國公債短端殖利率上揚，油價下跌則支撐長天期債券。10年期通膨補償下降2.4個基點，抵銷實質殖利率上升，名目殖利率幾乎未變。Williams仍傾向緊縮；美國PMI放緩與芝加哥聯準銀行活動指數低於趨勢，則增添景氣降溫跡象。$690億2年期公債標售投標倍數提高，得標殖利率低於發行前交易水準。

section_summaries.market_read: 市場重新肯定Nvidia領導層，使AI信用疑慮緩解；能否把合約需求轉為運作中的基礎設施與現金流，仍是償債能力的核心。
section_summaries.next_check: 若市場條件許可，Firmus可能在年底前嘗試發債；融資細節與最終條款仍待確定。
section_summaries.section_title: AI信用風險緩解，企業持續籌資
section_summaries.summary: 黃仁勳回任帶動AI信用市場反彈，CoreWeave的2032年到期債券價格上漲2.5美分。Firmus Grid正考慮發行約$15億債券，納入可能高達約$40億的債務方案，低於先前$75億的目標。Anthropic的$350億私人信貸安排，以及Meta的$125.5億專案融資，呈現AI資本需求的規模與融資方式的多樣性。港務局12月借款則增加了另一項基礎設施融資需求。

section_summaries.section_title: 法國推財政規則，歐洲成長分化
section_summaries.summary: 馬克宏提出透過修憲邁向財政平衡，帶動法國公債表現優於同業；據報法德10年期利差收窄5個基點至152個基點。德國綜合PMI增強，法國工廠產出則轉弱。西班牙反對黨的稅制與投資計畫，以勝選和財政審計為前提。英國活動放緩之際，Pill呼籲抑制通膨；加拿大實質報酬債市場縮小，則促使一家大型退休基金轉向美國TIPS。

section_summaries.market_read: Irca收購協議不以取得融資為成交前提；若CVC在債務承諾到期後被要求完成交易，可能須另覓資金或動用股權資金。
section_summaries.next_check: Irca將於11月26日公布財報，12月3日舉行債券持有人電話會議；收購融資承諾問題仍未解決。
section_summaries.section_title: 重整與併購爭議牽動債權安排
section_summaries.summary: CVC試圖退出收購後，Irca的收購融資銀行仍承諾提供€12億，這筆融資因而受CVC與Advent之間的契約爭議牽動。HX Expeditions取得債券持有人暫緩行使權利至2027年2月15日，同時可能在第二季出現資金缺口。Braskem與債權人就主要重整條款達成協議，包括股東注資$13億及$36億債轉股，細節與法院展延仍待處理。

section_summaries.next_check: 塞內加爾總統自12月2日起可解散國會，可能在預算爭議中開啟提前選舉的途徑。
section_summaries.section_title: 巴西預測惡化，各國主權融資分歧
section_summaries.summary: 巴西經濟學家調查將2027年底Selic利率預測上調至13%、通膨上調至5.12%，政府預測也轉向成長較弱、通膨較高。塞內加爾支付2033年到期債券票息，但預算衝突限制擬議中的$22億IMF計畫。奈及利亞匯率壓力反映證券投資資金外流與選舉不確定性。印度製造業增強、服務業轉弱；匈牙利對寬鬆釋出審慎訊號，以色列則在匯率與政治風險下維持政策利率3.25%。
美國就業與信心數據公布後，週三將密集發布PCE、支出、GDP與耐久財數據，檢驗重新回升的12月緊縮預期。週二5年期標售接續需求強勁的2年期標售，隨後感恩節將縮減交易時間。Irca資訊揭露、Braskem條款與Firmus融資，各有待落實的信用問題；西班牙大選、法國修憲提案與塞內加爾預算爭議，則分別考驗不同的財政落實途徑。
